questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

No carrots are beets.

Some carrots are gingers.

Some gingers are beets.

**Conclusions:**

I. All beets are gingers.

II. Some gingers are carrots.

III. Some beets are carrots.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cc617ab90fe5f630716fdff2d12345999229cdb4fde0f82b11304488dfb6049b.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All beets are gingers. → Does not follow (As, Some gingers are beets, which means some beets are gingers)

II. Some gingers are carrots. → **Follows** (As, Some carrots are gingers, which means Some gingers are carrots)

III. Some beets are carrots. → Does not follow (As, No carrots are beets, which means no beets are carrots)

Hence, ‘**Only conclusion II follows**’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which of the following is a secondary sector activity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Manufacturing.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Secondary sector activities involve the processing of raw materials extracted from the primary sector into finished goods. Manufacturing is a classic example of a secondary sector activity.**
 
• **Mining, quarrying, and forestry are primary sector** activities that involve the extraction of natural resources directly from the earth. These activities are important for providing the raw materials necessary for secondary sector activities.
 
• **Manufacturing **involves the** transformation of raw materials **into finished goods using various processes such as machining, welding, assembling, and packaging. This sector is crucial for economic development and job creation.
 
• **Secondary sector activities are often energy-intensive and require a significant amount of capital investment** in machinery, equipment, and infrastructure.
 
• Other examples of secondary sector activities include construction, utilities, and transportation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mining involves the extraction of minerals **and other valuable resources from the earth's crust. It is a major primary sector activity that provides raw materials for various secondary sector activities such as manufacturing and construction.
 
• **Forestry involves the cultivation, management, and harvesting of trees** and other vegetation for commercial purposes such as timber, pulp, and paper production. It is another primary sector activity that provides raw materials for various secondary sector activities.
 
• **Quarrying involves the extraction of rocks and minerals **from quarries or open-pit mines. It is a subset of mining and is primarily used for the extraction of building materials such as stone, gravel, and sand.

questions.question: What are Kho-Kho players sitting in the squares called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chasers.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kho-Kho players sitting in the squares are called Chasers.**
 
• **Chasers are responsible for chasing and tagging the runners to get them out.**
 
• Runners are the players who run around the field trying to avoid being tagged by the chasers.
 
• **Active Chasers** are the players who are currently chasing the runners.
 
• **The game of KHO KHO is one of the oldest traditional tag games in India. It is a team game.**
 
• 9 players will take the field in the beginning to start the match and 3 defenders of the opposite team try to avoid being touched by the chasers.
 
• It is a high-energy game that involves running and chasing.
 
• The motive of the sitting team is to "tag" the opponents.
 
• Blockers are the players who stand in the way of the chasers to protect the runners.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The origin of Kho-Kho is very difficult to trace, but many historians believe that it is a modified form of** 'Tag'/'Catch',** which in its simplest form involves chasing and touching a person.
 
• Originating in Maharashtra**, Kho-Kho** in ancient times was played on** 'raths' or chariots and was known as Rathera.**
 
• The present appearance of the game was an adoption from the time of World War I in 1914.
 
• The Deccan Gymkhana club of Pune, Maharashtra so named and baptized by the great Indian leader Lokmanya Tilak & Bhai Narorkar drafted the first-ever rules and regulations that symbolized the metamorphosis of the game soon to follow.

questions.question: GNP stands for ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a__** **____**gross national product.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​GNP - Gross National Product.__
 
• It is the total value of all the final products and services in a given period in terms of production by a country's residents.
 
• It is calculated by taking the sum of personal consumption expenditures, domestic investment, expenditure by government, net exports, and any income earned by residents from overseas investments, and deducting the income earned within the domestic economy by foreign residents.
 
• GDP is Gross Domestic Product. It is the national output produced in a country.
 
• GNP = GDP + net property income from abroad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• GDP is the final value of all the goods and services produced in a country in a given year.
 
• The nominal gross domestic product is the gross domestic product (GDP) evaluated at current market prices.
 
• Real GDP, on the other hand, is calculated by taking a base year as a determinant.
 
• Real GDP adjusts for price changes due to inflation/deflation.
 
• The main difference between nominal GDP and real GDP is the adjustment for inflation.

questions.question: Three milk bottles of 1 litre, 750 millilitres and 650 millilitres with milk percentage respectively 45%, 50% and 60% are emptied in a same container simultaneously. What is the percentage of milk in the mixture?
questions.solution:
**Given values:**

Volume of first milk bottle: 1L with 45% milk.

Volume of second milk bottle: 750ml with 50% milk.

Volume of third milk bottle: 650ml with 60% milk.

**The concept used:** The percentage of milk in the mixture is the total amount of milk divided by the total volume.

**Solution:**

Calculate the total amount of milk: (1 × 0.45) + (0.75 × 0.50) + (0.65 × 0.60).

Calculate the total volume: 1 + 0.75 + 0.65.

Calculate the percentage: (Total milk/Total volume) × 100.

⇒ Total milk = (1 × 0.45) + (0.75 × 0.50) + (0.65 × 0.60) = 0.45 + 0.375 + 0.39 = 1.215L

⇒ Total volume = 1 + 0.75 + 0.65 = 2.4L

⇒ Percentage of milk = (1.215 / 2.4) × 100 = 50.625%

**Therefore, the percentage of milk in the mixture is 50.625%.**

questions.question: A cop sees a thief at a distance of 120 m. He starts chasing the thief who is running at a speed of 6 m/sec. The cop is chasing him with a speed of 8 m/sec. Find the distance covered by the thief before the cop catches him.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Initial distance between cop and thief: 120 m

Speed of thief: 6 m/sec

Speed of cop: 8 m/sec

**Concept used:

Relative speed is the difference of individual speeds, and the distance covered by the thief before the cop catches him is the product of the thief's speed and the time it takes for the cop to catch him.

Solution:**

Calculate the relative speed: 8 m/sec - 6 m/sec.

Calculate the time for the cop to catch the thief: 120 m / relative speed.

Calculate the distance covered by the thief: thief's speed * time.

⇒ Relative speed = 8 m/sec - 6 m/sec = 2 m/sec

⇒ Time = 120 m / 2 m/sec = 60 sec

⇒ Distance covered by the thief = 6 m/sec × 60 sec = 360 m

**Therefore, the thief covers a distance of 360 m before the cop catches him.**

questions.question: A police officer follows a thief who is at a distance of 800 m from him. If they run at the speeds of 8 km/h and 7 km/h, respectively, what distance (in metre) does the police officer run to catch the thief?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When time is constant, the ratio of distances traveled is directly proportional to the ratio of their speeds.

Ratio of distances (Police : Thief) = 8 : 7

Difference in distance covered = 8 − 7 = 1 unit

Since the initial gap is 800 m, 1 unit = 800 m

Distance run by police officer = 8 units = 8 × 800 = 6400 m

**∴ The correct answer is 6400 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**
